title: The gym-owner site and the members' notice say member data is kept in India, but a full nightly copy sits with Cloudflare outside that promise
what: The gym-owner website says 'Your member data is stored in India' and 'Data kept in India (Mumbai)', and the short notice gyms copy for their members says MettleUp has 'servers in Mumbai, India'. But every night a full readable copy of the gym database is written to Cloudflare's store for 7 days, and the privacy notice itself lists Cloudflare's location as 'many countries, including India'. The web server's own small database (payment records, form questions) has no India location set either.
expected: The words match where the data really is: either keep the nightly copy and the web database in India, or say plainly that a backup copy is kept with Cloudflare, which may store it outside India.
how_often: every time someone reads the page; the copy is made every night
fix_line: Change the words to name the Cloudflare backup copy, or keep the backup in an India-only store

title: The join form and the gym page's question and AI boxes say 'Only this gym sees' your details, but others do too
what: The online join form says 'Only {gym} sees your details', and the gym web page's question box and the AI helper's 'leave your number' box say 'Only this gym sees them'. In fact MettleUp's server keeps them, the payment company gets the name and number when a person pays online, and every AI helper message has already been read by Anthropic's AI (the AI helper is still switched off, so this matters when it is turned on).
expected: Say who else handles the details in one short line, for example 'Sent to {gym}. MettleUp keeps them safely for the gym', and on the AI box say an AI company reads the questions, with the privacy link next to it.
who: people joining online or asking a gym from its web page
fix_line: Rewrite the 'only this gym sees' lines to name MettleUp, the payment company and the AI company where they apply

title: The About page calls the gym's app a 'desk app', while every other page calls it the admin app
what: The About page says gyms get 'a desk app for members, plans, renewals...'. The gym-owner site, the delivery page, the terms and the installed app's own name all call it the admin app (or MettleUp Admin). A payment company or owner reading About meets a third name for the same thing.
who: gym owners and payment company reviewers
fix_line: Change 'a desk app' to 'the admin app' on the About page

items.reason: the public pages have no save-settings button; the gym page editor lives in the admin app
